text:
incident-bot: PAGER -> ALB unhealthy / Envoy connreset spike in euc1b (approx 04:11 UTC). Trigger: ALB target-group unhealthy count > 30% and ingress 5xx surge. Paging oncall.

maria.sre: seeing a sharp jump in backend 502/504s from envoy proxies in euc1b. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/infra/dashboards/ingress-euc1b (errors ~18% -> 62% in last 5m)

raj.oncall: on it. I’ll gather quick impact and start triage. Any recent deploys to ingress or control plane? :eyes:

deploy-bot: Recent deploys: service/ingress-controller rolled at 03:58 UTC to euc1b (canary), rollout completed 04:05 UTC. No other infra deploys in the window.

kevin-net: networking note — Route53 health checks for euc1b ALBs toggled earlier today during routine test window, but nothing scheduled near 04:10. I’ll check ALB target group metrics and NLB peers.

maria.sre: logs show repeated TLS handshake failures and ECONNRESET between ALB -> envoy (backend). Example from envoy logs:
```
[2026-02-28T04:09:34Z] connection terminated: error=EOF remote_addr=10.12.45.122:443
[2026-02-28T04:09:34Z] upstream reset: connection failure, reason=connection reset by peer
```

maria.sre: also seeing the node-level conntrack exhaustion on a subset of nodes (euc1b-worker-*) — nf_conntrack_count nearing threshold on 3 hosts.

raj.oncall: conntrack exhaustion would cause resets. Are we hitting a sudden burst of short-lived connections? Any change in keepalive/windows from ALB side?

kevin-net: ALB target connection settings default keepalive still on. But health checks show lots of 503 from envoy/ingress. Could be a combination of worker oom/evictions or proxy fast-fail.

jordan-platform: I’m pulling node metrics and kube events. Running kubectl --namespace ingress get pods -o wide on the affected ASG.

jordan-platform: Found repeated Pod restarts for ingress-controller on nodes euc1b-*. CrashLoop backoff spikes on two pods started ~04:07.

maria.sre: ok that explains backend resets. Root cause likely ingress controller instability + conntrack exhaustion under load. Next steps: scale ingress replicas, cordon+drain the two noisy nodes, and put a temporary routing fallback to NLB in another AZ.

raj.oncall: Agreed. Quick mitigation plan:
1) Scale ingress-controller replicas from 3 -> 7 in euc1b
2) Cordon & drain nodes euc1b-02 and euc1b-08 and restart kube-proxy on them
3) Increase conntrack max on nodes (sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max) via daemonset rollout
4) Temporarily update ALB routing weight to favor euc1a/euc1c (manual DNS weight shift) to reduce incoming traffic to euc1b

tina-support: Heads-up to support: likely customer impact for ~euc1b-only customers. I’ll draft a customer-safe status update after we confirm mitigation.

kevin-net: while scaling, also enabling ALB idle timeout bump from 60 -> 120s for target group as a precaution.

raj.oncall: executing step 1 now.

raj.oncall: kubectl scale deploy/ingress-controller --replicas=7 -n ingress

maria.sre: I’ll watch pod readiness and LB target registration.

jordan-platform: draining node euc1b-02 now: kubectl cordon/evict. Draining will take ~45s for active connections.

incident-bot: NOTE: On-call handoff scheduled. Current pager: raj.oncall (primary) -> backup: maria.sre in 30m.

kevin-net: increased target group idle timeout and altered ALB weight: routing shifts 60%->euc1a/euc1c, 40%->euc1b. This should reduce pressure. Watch for traffic shift anomalies.

maria.sre: after scale, pod restarts decreased, envoy reset rate dropped from 1200/min -> 220/min over 5m. Conntrack count per-node also dropping after drain/restarts.

raj.oncall: sysctl applied via daemonset (rolled to 80% nodes): net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144

jordan-platform: kube-proxy restarted on euc1b-08. No more crashloops observed there.

tina-support: ETA for customer update? If we can confirm error rate <5% and stable for 10m I’ll push the status message.

maria.sre: we’re at 3.8% 5xx across the region, euc1b specifically 6.2%. Traffic weighting continues to shift. Recommend wait 10 more minutes then post.

raj.oncall: agree. Keeping incident in active mitigation. Filing an incident ticket and assigning severity S2 for partial region outage.

tina-support: Drafted status: "We’re aware of increased errors affecting some customers in the euc1b region due to load balancer/ingress instability. Our engineers are actively mitigating; a portion of traffic is being routed to healthy AZs. We’ll update in 30 minutes or as we confirm recovery." Ready to post pending timeline.

maria.sre: note for postmortem — check ingress controller memory spikes, kube-proxy conntrack handling, and ALB healthcheck surge sensitivity. Also correlate with the canary deploy earlier.

raj.oncall: will escalate to eng-runtime if we see recurrence after rollback window; also capture flame graphs of ingress controller around crash time.

deploy-bot: Rollback option available: ingress-controller v2.4.1 -> v2.4.0. Rollback flag: --rollback=true

kevin-net: recommendation: after stability, revert ALB weight back to normal once conntrack and pods healthy. Also consider increasing connection re-use settings on envoy/proxy.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation in progress. Primary oncall: raj.oncall, backup: maria.sre. Status: degraded (partial regional impact). Next update scheduled in 10m.

maria.sre: after 12m from mitigation start, error rate in euc1b down to 2.1%. All ingress pods stable. Marking mitigation successful. Proceeding to gradual revert of ALB weights and scale replicas back to desired (5).

raj.oncall: initiating scale down to 5 replicas and reverting ALB weight to even distribution.

tina-support: Posting status update now. Copy of message: "Services have recovered in euc1b; routing was temporarily shifted to healthy AZs and additional replicas were provisioned. Monitoring continues. If you see residual errors please reach out." :white_check_mark:

maria.sre: creating incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime + platform for full RCA. Initial impacts: ~40 minutes of elevated errors, peak 62% 5xx in euc1b, approx 11% of total customer requests affected at peak.

raj.oncall: handing off to maria.sre for postmortem and follow-up. I’ll update oncall notes and close the active pager.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: Active page closed for raj.oncall. New owner: maria.sre. Incident channel archived in 2h for postmortem notes.

maria.sre: thanks all. Will surface a timeline, root cause hypothesis, and action items in postmortem (link will be posted here). If anyone has logs or traces not in the main folder, please upload to /mnt/incidents/2154009876.

tina-support: filing customer follow-up list for outreach. Noting top 5 impacted accounts for support to contact.

kevin-net: adding follow-up ticket to infra backlog: increase default conntrack on workers, improve ALB healthcheck smoothing, and investigate ingress canary isolation.

maria.sre: closing thread summary: mitigation steps taken, impact, next steps assigned. Will post the final postmortem within 48h.
